claim: HIV-1 itself cannot replicate in murine cells, even when they are engineered to express human versions of HIV-1 receptors and essential Tat cofactors that enable HIV-1 entry and transcription in murine cells.
source: HIV-1 itself cannot replicate in murine cells, even when they are engineered to expressed human versions of HIV-1 receptors and essential Tat cofactors that enable HIV-1 entry and transcription in murine cells (Bieniasz and Cullen, 2000; Mariani et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work (Bieniasz and Cullen, 2000; Mariani et al., 2000).

claim: VSV has a very broad tropism.
source: However, VSV has a very broad tropism and numerous VSV-based chimeric viruses expressing functional, heterologous envelope proteins, including that of HIV-1, have been generated (Boritz et al., 1999; Johnson et al., 1997; Rabinovich et al., 2014; Rose et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work (Boritz et al., 1999; Johnson et al., 1997; Rabinovich et al., 2014; Rose et al., 2001).

claim: Numerous VSV-based chimeric viruses expressing functional, heterologous envelope proteins, including that of HIV-1, have been generated.
source: However, VSV has a very broad tropism and numerous VSV-based chimeric viruses expressing functional, heterologous envelope proteins, including that of HIV-1, have been generated (Boritz et al., 1999; Johnson et al., 1997; Rabinovich et al., 2014; Rose et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior published work (Boritz et al., 1999; Johnson et al., 1997; Rabinovich et al., 2014; Rose et al., 2001).

claim: RhIV strains were generated encoding Env proteins from diverse HIV-1 strains including HIV-1NL4-3, HIV-1ADA, and HIV-1AD17.
source: Initially we constructed RhIV strains encoding the subtype B Env proteins of HIV-1NL4-3, a laboratory adapted X4-tropic strain, HIV-1ADA, a macrophage tropic primary isolate and HIV-1AD17, an R5 tropic transmitted founder (T/F) HIV-1 strain.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text describing the construction of RhIV strains.

claim: The ectodomain and transmembrane domains of HIV-1 Env were fused to the cytoplasmic tail of VSV-G in RhIV constructs.
source: The ectodomain and transmembrane domains of HIV-1 Env were fused to the cytoplasmic tail of VSV-G (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A showing the schematic representation of RhIV genomes.

claim: Retaining the VSV-G cytoplasmic tail has the potential to perturb the tertiary structure of the HIV-1 ectodomain.
source: Retaining the VSV-G cytoplasmic tail has the potential to perturb the tertiary structure of the HIV-1 ectodomain, but this strategy improves HIV-1 Env incorporation into VSV particles (Johnson et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is stated as a potential consequence and is supported by a citation (Johnson et al., 1997).

claim: Retaining the VSV-G cytoplasmic tail improves HIV-1 Env incorporation into VSV particles.
source: Retaining the VSV-G cytoplasmic tail has the potential to perturb the tertiary structure of the HIV-1 ectodomain, but this strategy improves HIV-1 Env incorporation into VSV particles (Johnson et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior published work (Johnson et al., 1997).

claim: HIV-1 envelope protein was readily detectable in lysates from RhIVADA infected cells and pelleted virions.
source: Western blot analysis of RhIVADA showed that the HIV-1 envelope protein was readily detectable in lysates from infected cells and pelleted virions (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: RhIVNL4-3 and RhIVAD17 strains displayed the appropriate receptor specificity when used to infect GHOSTX4 or GHOSTR5 cells.
source: RhIVNL4-3 and RhIVAD17 strains displayed the appropriate receptor specificity when used to infect GHOSTX4 or GHOSTR5 cells (Figure 1C)
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Infection of GHOSTX4 or GHOSTR5 cells with RhIV, but not VSV, led to the appearance of large syncytia, in addition to a pronounced cytopathic effect.
source: infection of these cells with RhIV, but not VSV, led to the appearance of large syncytia, in addition to a pronounced cytopathic effect (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images shown in Figure 1C.

claim: A panel of RhIV constructs expressing a variety of physiologically relevant envelope proteins from HIV-1 clades A, B, and C, including T/F viruses, replicated well in vitro, reaching titers of ~106 to 107 plaque forming units (PFU)/ml.
source: We therefore generated a larger panel of RhIV constructs expressing a variety of physiologically relevant envelope proteins from HIV-1 clades A, B, and C, including T/F viruses. All of these viruses replicated well in vitro, reaching titers of ~106 to 107 plaque forming units (PFU)/ml (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: RhIVAD17(GFP) replicated robustly in GHOSTR5 cells, generating green fluorescent syncytia.
source: RhIVAD17(GFP) replicated robustly in GHOSTR5 cells, generating green fluorescent syncytia, as well as in a human T-cell line MT2/R5 engineered to express the CCR5 coreceptor (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images shown in Figure 1F.

claim: RhIVAD17(GFP) replicated robustly in MT2/R5 cells.
source: RhIVAD17(GFP) replicated robustly in GHOSTR5 cells, generating green fluorescent syncytia, as well as in a human T-cell line MT2/R5 engineered to express the CCR5 coreceptor (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Live imaging of RhIVAD17(GFP) replication in 293T/CD4/CCR5 cell monolayers suggested a dominant mode of viral spread in cell monolayers via direct cell-cell transmission, with additional viral transmission to distal cells.
source: Live imaging of RhIVAD17(GFP) replication in 293T/CD4/CCR5 cell monolayers suggested a dominant mode of viral spread in cell monolayers via direct cell-cell transmission, with additional viral transmission to distal cells (Video 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by live imaging data shown in Video 1.

claim: Infection of TZMbl cells with RhIVAD17(nLuc) generated high levels of nLuc within a few hours of infection.
source: Infection of TZMbl cells (a popular target cell for HIV-1 neutralization assays) with RhIVAD17(nLuc) generated high levels of nLuc within a few hours of infection (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Sensitivity to the CCR5-binding antagonist maraviroc was similar for each HIV-1 envelope in the context of either HIV-1 or RhIV infection.
source: Analysis of a panel of RhIV (nLuc) and corresponding HIV-1 (nLuc) viruses revealed that sensitivity to the CCR5-binding antagonist maraviroc was similar for each HIV-1 envelope in the context of either HIV-1 or RhIV infection (Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Matched RhIV (nLuc) and HIV-1 (nLuc) viruses exhibited similar neutralization properties.
source: In general, matched RhIV (nLuc) and HIV-1 (nLuc) viruses exhibited similar neutralization properties (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by neutralization data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Most RhIV and HIV-1 strains were sensitive to the quaternary epitope targeting PG16 and PG9 antibodies.
source: While most RhIV and HIV-1 strains were sensitive to the quaternary epitope targeting PG16 and PG9 antibodies, the RhIV1054/HIV-11054, RhIVSF162/HIV-1SF162 and RhIV V1/HIV-1V1 virus pairs each shared the property of being resistant to PG9 and PG16 (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by neutralization data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: The RhIV1054/HIV-11054, RhIVSF162/HIV-1SF162 and RhIV V1/HIV-1V1 virus pairs each shared the property of being resistant to PG9 and PG16.
source: While most RhIV and HIV-1 strains were sensitive to the quaternary epitope targeting PG16 and PG9 antibodies, the RhIV1054/HIV-11054, RhIVSF162/HIV-1SF162 and RhIV V1/HIV-1V1 virus pairs each shared the property of being resistant to PG9 and PG16 (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by neutralization data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: The HIV-1V1 strain exhibited near complete resistance to all bNAbs tested, except 10–1074.
source: The HIV-1V1 strain was unusual in exhibiting near complete resistance to all bNAbs tested, except 10–1074 and this property was preserved in the corresponding RhIVV1 chimeric virus (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by neutralization data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The property of near complete resistance to all bNAbs tested, except 10–1074, was preserved in the RhIVV1 chimeric virus.
source: The HIV-1V1 strain was unusual in exhibiting near complete resistance to all bNAbs tested, except 10–1074 and this property was preserved in the corresponding RhIVV1 chimeric virus (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by neutralization data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The MPER-targeting bNAb (10E8) neutralized RhIVCH505 but did not neutralize HIV-1CH505.
source: In one example, the MPER-targeting bNAb (10E8) neutralized RhIVCH505 but did not neutralize HIV-1CH505 (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by neutralization data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Discrepancies in the potencies with which matched HIV-1 (nLuc) and RhIV (nLuc) viruses were neutralized by bNAbs may be the result of the HIV-1 and VSV-G cytoplasmic tails imposing different conformations on the Env ectodomain.
source: These occasional discrepancies may be the result of the HIV-1 and VSV-G cytoplasmic tails imposing different conformations on the Env ectodomain.
evidence: The claim is stated as a possible explanation for observed discrepancies.

claim: There may be differences in Env spike density, heterogeneity and distribution on RhIV virions as compared to HIV-1 virions.
source: Alternatively there may be differences in Env spike density, heterogeneity and distribution on RhIV virions as compared to HIV-1 virions.
evidence: The claim is stated as an alternative possible explanation for observed discrepancies.

claim: Transgenic mice were generated that express human CD4 and CCR5 exclusively on murine CD4-positive cells.
source: In parallel, we constructed transgenic mice that express human CD4 and CCR5, exclusively in mouse CD4-positive cells, at levels mimicking those on human CD4+ T-cells.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the generation of transgenic mice.

claim: Transgenic mice express human CD4 and CCR5 at levels mimicking those on human CD4+ T-cells.
source: In parallel, we constructed transgenic mice that express human CD4 and CCR5, exclusively in mouse CD4-positive cells, at levels mimicking those on human CD4+ T-cells.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the generation of transgenic mice.

claim: The A1 line mimicked the levels of hCD4 found on human CD4+ T-cells.
source: The A1 line mimicked the levels of hCD4 found on human CD4+ T-cells (Figure 3C) and was used in subsequent experiments unless otherwise indicated.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Levels of CCR5 on the CD4+ cells in the A1 mice were similar to levels of CCR5 on human CD4+ cells.
source: Levels of CCR5 (as indicated by fluorescence intensity) on the CD4+ cells in the A1 mice were also similar to levels of CCR5 on human CD4+ cells.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the characterization of the A1 mouse line.

claim: ~100% of hCD4+ cells in the blood of A1 mice were CCR5+.
source: However, as expected ~100% of hCD4+ cells in the blood of A1 mice were CCR5+ (Figure 3D), while the fraction of CD4+ T-cells that also express CCR5 is known to vary according to tissue location in humans (see discussion).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: hCD4, like mouse CD4, was expressed exclusively on CD3+ cells, but was absent from the CD8+ cell fraction.
source: FACS analysis revealed that hCD4, like mouse CD4, was expressed exclusively on CD3+ cells, but was absent from the CD8+ cell fraction (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: 100% of mouse CD4+ cells (but no other cells) in A1 mice expressed hCD4 and CCR5 at levels mimicking human CD4+ T-cells.
source: Overall, 100% of mouse CD4+ cells (but no other cells) in A1 mice expressed hCD4 and CCR5 at levels mimicking human CD4+ T-cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: VSV is extremely sensitive to type-1 interferon.
source: Because VSV is extremely sensitive to type-1 interferon (Müller et al., 1994), we crossed A1, C18 and B4 mice to C57BL/6 mice lacking the type one interferon receptor gene (Ifnar1), generating A1Ifnar-/-, C18Ifnar-/- and B4Ifnar-/- lines.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior published work (Müller et al., 1994).

claim: Infection of A1Ifnar-/- mice with 105 PFU of RhIVCH505 resulted in profound and selective depletion of CD4+ T-cells 4 days later.
source: We first infected A1Ifnar-/- mice with 105 PFU of RhIVCH505 by intraperitoneal injection (i.p.). FACS analysis of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) 4 days later revealed profound and selective depletion of CD4+ T-cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Infection of A1Ifnar-/- mice with 105 PFU of RhIVCH505 resulted in progressive and profound reductions in CD4+ T-cell numbers in PBMC and spleen.
source: Next, we infected a cohort of A1Ifnar-/- mice with 105 PFU of RhIVCH505 and measured CD4+ T-cell numbers and viral RNA levels in lymphoid tissues. This analysis revealed progressive and profound reductions in CD4+ T-cell numbers in PBMC and spleen, and near complete depletion of CD4+ T-cells from thymus and lymph nodes (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Infection of A1Ifnar-/- mice with 105 PFU of RhIVCH505 resulted in near complete depletion of CD4+ T-cells from thymus and lymph nodes.
source: Next, we infected a cohort of A1Ifnar-/- mice with 105 PFU of RhIVCH505 and measured CD4+ T-cell numbers and viral RNA levels in lymphoid tissues. This analysis revealed progressive and profound reductions in CD4+ T-cell numbers in PBMC and spleen, and near complete depletion of CD4+ T-cells from thymus and lymph nodes (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Viral RNA levels peaked at between 103 and 106 copies/μg of cellular RNA between day 1 and day 4 after infection, depending on the tissue.
source: Viral RNA levels peaked at between 103 and 106 copies/μg of cellular RNA between day 1 and day 4 after infection, depending on the tissue, with the highest levels (>106 copies/μg) found in thymus (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The highest levels of viral RNA (>106 copies/μg) were found in thymus.
source: Viral RNA levels peaked at between 103 and 106 copies/μg of cellular RNA between day 1 and day 4 after infection, depending on the tissue, with the highest levels (>106 copies/μg) found in thymus (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Plasma viremia peaked at between 106 and 108 RNA copies/ml on day 1 after infection with RhIV strains.
source: Plasma viremia peaked at between 106 and 108 RNA copies/ml on day 1 after infection, then declined rapidly during days 1–7 and was cleared before day 14 (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Plasma viremia declined rapidly during days 1–7 and was cleared before day 14 after RhIV infection.
source: Plasma viremia peaked at between 106 and 108 RNA copies/ml on day 1 after infection, then declined rapidly during days 1–7 and was cleared before day 14 (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: CD4+ T cells were nearly completely depleted from blood by day 4 after RhIV infection, then gradually recovered.
source: CD4+ T cells were nearly completely depleted from blood by day 4, then gradually recovered (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Infection of A1Ifnar-/- mice with 103 PFU of RhIV strains established robust infection with profound CD4+ T-cell depletion, albeit with reduced peak plasma viremia (105–107 RNA copies/ml).
source: Infection of A1Ifnar-/- mice with reduced doses of RhIVBG505, RhIVDu156, RhIVSF162, or RhIVCH505 revealed that 103 PFU established robust infection with profound CD4+ T-cell depletion, albeit with reduced peak plasma viremia (105–107 RNA copies/ml, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Infection of immunocompetent (A1Ifnar+/+) mice with 105 PFU of RhIVBG505, RhIVDu156, or RhIVSF162 yielded robust infection albeit with ~10 to 100-fold reduced peak viremia as compared to A1Ifnar-/- mice.
source: Infection of immunocompetent (A1Ifnar+/+) mice with 105 PFU of RhIVBG505, RhIVDu156, or RhIVSF162 yielded robust infection albeit with ~10 to 100-fold reduced peak viremia as compared to A1Ifnar-/- mice, (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: RhIVSF162 appeared to cause more profound CD4+ T-cell depletion than RhIVBG505 and RhIVDu156 in A1Ifnar+/+ mice, despite reaching similar or lower levels of plasma viremia.
source: A1Ifnar+/+ mice also revealed apparent differences in the ability of RhIV strains to cause CD4+ T-cell depletion that did not correlate with differences in plasma viremia. RhIVSF162 appeared to cause more profound CD4+ T-cell depletion than RhIVBG505 and RhIVDu156, despite reaching similar or lower levels of plasma viremia (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The RhIVCH505 strain exhibited exquisite sensitivity to CD4 expression levels.
source: The RhIVCH505 strain, bearing a T/F HIV-1 Env protein, exhibited exquisite sensitivity to CD4 expression levels.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the sensitivity of RhIVCH505 to CD4 expression levels.

claim: Infection of C18Ifnar-/- mice with RhIVCH505 resulted in 1000-fold lower peak viremia compared to A1Ifnar-/- mice.
source: Infection of C18Ifnar-/- mice resulted in 1000-fold lower peak viremia compared to A1Ifnar-/- mice, while B4Ifnar-/- mice appeared completely resistant to RhIVCH505 infection (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: B4Ifnar-/- mice appeared completely resistant to RhIVCH505 infection.
source: Infection of C18Ifnar-/- mice resulted in 1000-fold lower peak viremia compared to A1Ifnar-/- mice, while B4Ifnar-/- mice appeared completely resistant to RhIVCH505 infection (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The RhIVADA strain was comparatively insensitive to variation in CD4 expression levels.
source: Conversely, the RhIVADA strain that bears a macrophage tropic HIV-1 Env protein was comparatively insensitive to variation in CD4 expression levels.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the sensitivity of RhIVADA to CD4 expression levels.

claim: Infection of A1Ifnar-/- and C18Ifnar-/- mice with RhIVADA gave approximately equivalent peak viremia.
source: Indeed, infection of A1Ifnar-/- and C18Ifnar-/- mice gave approximately equivalent peak viremia, while infection of B4Ifnar-/- mice gave peak viremia that was reduced only ~10 fold compared to the other mouse lines (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Infection of B4Ifnar-/- mice with RhIVADA gave peak viremia that was reduced only ~10 fold compared to A1Ifnar-/- and C18Ifnar-/- mice.
source: Indeed, infection of A1Ifnar-/- and C18Ifnar-/- mice gave approximately equivalent peak viremia, while infection of B4Ifnar-/- mice gave peak viremia that was reduced only ~10 fold compared to the other mouse lines (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: RhIV infection was apparently cleared in all cases.
source: Although infection of A1Ifnar-/- mice, and in some cases A1Ifnar+/+ mice, led to high level viremia and profound CD4+ T-cell depletion, in all cases RhIV infection was apparently cleared.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the outcome of RhIV infection.

claim: CD4+ T-cells exhibited near complete recovery by approximately 40 to 50 days after initial RhIVCH505 infection in A1Ifnar-/- mice.
source: Long term follow-up of a group of RhIVCH505-infected A1Ifnar-/- mice showed that CD4+ T-cells exhibited near complete recovery by approximately 40 to 50 days after initial infection (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: PG16 and 3BNC117 antibodies appeared to provide sterilizing protection against RhIVBG505 infection in A1Ifnar+/+ mice.
source: Both antibodies appeared to provide sterilizing protection, in that no viral RNA was detected in plasma of antibody-injected mice and no perturbations in CD4+ T-cells were observed (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The highest dose of 3BNC117 (1 mg) gave apparently sterilizing protection against RhIVCH505 infection in A1Ifnar-/- mice.
source: As was the case with RhIVBG505, the highest dose of 3BNC117 gave apparently sterilizing protection against RhIVCH505 infection, with undetectable plasma viremia and no CD4+ cell depletion (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: At 0.5 mg 3BNC117, 2/3 mice exhibited apparently sterile protection against RhIVCH505, while a third had barely detectable viremia and minimal CD4+ T-cell depletion.
source: At 0.5 mg 3BNC117, 2/3 mice exhibited apparently sterile protection, while a third had barely detectable viremia and minimal CD4+ T-cell depletion.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the results of antibody protection experiments.

claim: At lower 3BNC117 doses (50 μg and 100 μg), partial protection was observed against RhIVCH505, with low-level viremia (<103 copies/ml) and clear CD4+ T-cell depletion, that was not as extensive as control animals.
source: At lower 3BNC117 doses (50 μg and 100 μg), partial protection was observed, with low-level viremia (<103 copies/ml) and clear CD4+ T-cell depletion, that was not as extensive as control animals (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Following the second challenge with RhIVSF162, only low-level plasma viremia (~103 RNA copies/ml) was detected, and only in a subset of mice.
source: Following the second challenge, only low-level plasma viremia (~103 RNA copies/ml) was detected, and only in a subset of mice.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the results of rechallenge experiments.

claim: The magnitude of CD4+ T-cell depletion following the second RhIVSF162 infection was reduced compared to the first infection in A1Ifnar-/- mice.
source: The magnitude of CD4+ T-cell depletion following the second infection was reduced compared to the first infection (in A1Ifnar-/- mice) or absent (in A1Ifnar+/+ mice).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the results of rechallenge experiments.

claim: Following a third challenge with RhIVSF162, plasma viremia was undetectable, and only minor perturbations of CD4+T cell numbers were observed.
source: Following a third challenge with RhIVSF162 at 84 days (Expt#2) or 91 days (Expt#1 and Expt#3) after the first infection, plasma viremia was undetectable, and only minor perturbations of CD4+T cell numbers were observed (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Challenge of A1Ifnar+/+ mice with VSVMLV-E, 28 days after infection and clearance of RhIVBG505 resulted in no detectable plasma viremia.
source: Similarly, challenge of A1Ifnar+/+ mice with VSVMLV-E, 28 days after infection and clearance of RhIVBG505 resulted in no detectable plasma viremia (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Protection against RhIV infection, afforded by a prior RhIV infection, did not require an immune response to the HIV-1 envelope protein.
source: Given that MLV-E and HIV-1 Env proteins share no sequence similarity, these experiments suggested that the protection against RhIV infection, afforded by a prior RhIV infection (Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1) did not require an immune response to the HIV-1 envelope protein.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an inference from the VSVMLV-E experiments.

claim: A B-cell mediated immune response was not required for the vaccine effect of a prior RhIV infection on subsequent RhIV challenge.
source: Thus, a B-cell mediated immune response was not required for the vaccine effect of a prior RhIV infection on subsequent RhIV challenge.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a conclusion from experiments using B-cell deficient mice.

claim: A1Ifnar-/- mice infected three times with RhIVSF162 elicited antibodies that bound all four of the SOSIP envelope proteins tested.
source: A1Ifnar-/- mice infected three times with RhIVSF162 (subtype B, Expt #3) elicited antibodies that bound all four of the SOSIP envelope proteins, whose titers increased after the second infection (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A.

claim: ELISA titers were higher with the B41 (subtype B) and BG505 (subtype A) than with the two subtype C SOSIP proteins in mice infected three times with RhIVSF162.
source: ELISA titers were higher with the B41 (subtype B) and BG505 (subtype A) than with the two subtype C SOSIP proteins (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A), partly reflecting sequence similarity between the infecting RhIV strain and the ELISA antigens.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The second RhIV infection boosted and apparently broadened the antibody response initiated by the first RhIV infection.
source: However, all four SOSIP proteins were recognized and the second infection (RhIVBG505) boosted and apparently broadened the antibody response initiated by RhIVDu156 infection.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the antibody responses after sequential RhIV infections.

claim: A1Ifnar-/- mice generated higher titers of Env binding antibodies than A1Ifnar+/+ mice.
source: A1Ifnar-/- mice generated higher titers of Env binding antibodies than A1Ifnar+/+ mice, thus any potential deficit in antibody generation that might have resulted from the absence of type-I interferon signals was overwhelmed by the larger antigen load following infection (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The second and sometimes the third RhIV challenges with either homologous or heterologous RhIV strains increased titers and broadened ELISA reactivity.
source: The second and sometimes the third RhIV challenges with either homologous or heterologous RhIV strains increased titers and broadened ELISA reactivity (Figure 6—figure supplement 4A and B, Figure 6—figure supplement 5A,B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4A and B, Figure 6—figure supplement 5A,B.

claim: Broadly Env reactive binding antibodies were elicited after three RhIV infections, regardless of the RhIV stains used in the three challenges.
source: In most cases, broadly Env reactive binding antibodies were elicited after three RhIV infections, regardless of the RhIV stains used in the three challenges.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the antibody responses after three RhIV infections.

claim: Mouse sera from RhIV infected mice revealed prominent reactivity with epitope(s) on gp41 as well as gp120.
source: Further analysis of sera from a subset of mice challenged with a variety of RhIV strains (in Exp #5) using commercial antigen-loaded diagnostic reagents (INNO-LIA HIV I/II Score) revealed prominent reactivity with epitope(s) on gp41 as well as gp120 (Figure 6—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 6A.

claim: Mouse sera from RhIV infected mice did not contain detectable levels of antibodies that could compete with human bnAbs or sCD4 for binding to the CD4bs, the apex of the Env trimer formed by the V2 loop or a glycosylation dependent epitope in the V3 loop.
source: Notably, however, these mouse sera did not contain detectable levels of antibodies that could compete with human bnAbs or (sCD4) for binding to the CD4bs, the apex of the Env trimer formed by the V2 loop or a glycosylation dependent epitope in the V3 loop (Figure 6—figure supplement 6B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by competition ELISA data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 6B.

claim: In mice that had been challenged three times with RhIVSF162, weak neutralization activity was observed against HIV-1SF162, but not against a heterologous strain (HIV-1CH505).
source: In mice that had been challenged three times with RhIVSF162, (Expts #1–3) weak neutralization activity was observed against HIV-1SF162, but not against a heterologous strain (HIV-1CH505) (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by neutralization data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: In mice that were sequentially infected three times with RhIVDu156, RhIVBG505 and RhIVSF162, no neutralization was detected against HIV-1Du156, HIV-1BG505 or HIV-1SF162.
source: In mice that were sequentially infected three times with RhIVDu156, RhIVBG505 and RhIVSF162, (Expt #4) no neutralization was detected against HIV-1Du156, HIV-1BG505 or HIV-1SF162 (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by neutralization data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Three challenges with RhIVBG505 failed to elicit neutralizing activity against HIV-1BG505.
source: Even three challenges with RhIVBG505 failed to elicit neutralizing activity against HIV-1BG505.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text describing the neutralization results.

claim: RhIV infection elicited high titers of HIV-1 envelope binding antibodies that were primarily non-neutralizing.
source: Overall, RhIV infection elicited high titers of HIV-1 envelope binding antibodies. However, these antibodies were primarily non-neutralizing.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text summarizing the antibody responses to RhIV infection.
